Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The test case `testPrefixMapClear` creates a PatriciaTrie and fills it with several entries. Then it obtains a prefixMap view of the trie by calling `trie.prefixMap("And")`, returning a SortedMap view that represents all entries in the trie with keys starting with the prefix "And". The test then invokes `prefixMap.clear()`, which leads to a NullPointerException.

Inspecting `AbstractPatriciaTrie.prefixMap(K)` shows it calls `getPrefixMapByBits(K, int, int)` which returns a new `PrefixRangeMap` instance representing the prefix view.

The `PrefixRangeMap` is instantiated in `AbstractPatriciaTrie` as an inner class with prefix parameters and presumably provides a view onto the original PatriciaTrie filtered by prefix.

From experiment, the call to `prefixMap.clear()` leads to a NullPointerException, but removing entries individually works as a workaround.

This strongly suggests that the `PrefixRangeMap`'s implementation of `clear()` either is missing or improperly implemented, and dereferences a null value internally. Since `PrefixRangeMap` is a custom view, the `clear()` method probably tries to call a method or access a field that is null or uninitialized in the view context.

Because `prefixMap` returns a `SortedMap` view that delegates to inner PatriciaTrie data structures with prefix filtering, its `clear()` method should remove all prefix-matching entries. If `clear()` relies on internal structures or methods not set or not properly proxied in the `PrefixRangeMap`, a NullPointerException can occur.

Hence, the root cause is likely that the `PrefixRangeMap` class does not properly override the `clear()` method or the method's implementation incorrectly accesses internal or inherited state leading to null dereference.

Next, inspecting the `PrefixRangeMap` class's implementation of `clear()` (or its absence) will confirm this.

Overall, the failing test and bug report description, combined with code inspection, indicate that the `PrefixRangeMap.clear()` implementation leads to a NullPointerException because internal state or methods it relies on are null or improperly handled.

This diagnosis matches the symptoms of the failing test and the bug report's observation.

We should now examine the `PrefixRangeMap.clear()` method implementation in the `AbstractPatriciaTrie` class to locate the exact cause.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
